matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the abstract's absolute claim about eliminating artifacts is contradicted by the paper's own quantitative results (Table 1 FID scores and Table 3 error metrics showing non-zero transition errors).

Both identify inconsistencies in Table 1's results and the fairness of comparison. GT2 focuses on FID formatting/underline inconsistencies; pred_id 3 identifies the contradictory training conditions (500 vs 300 epochs) disclosed in the table note, both pointing to data integrity issues in Table 1.

Both identify a logical inconsistency in the phase mixing mechanism. GT3 notes that r=1 eliminates SPDM contribution contradicting progressive semantic enrichment; pred_id 7 identifies an undefined variable α in the same equation context that contradicts the described mixing process.

Both identify the same asymmetric training protocol issue: ACT-PAE was pre-trained on additional HumanML3D data while baselines used only BABEL-TEACH, creating an unfair advantage that contradicts the claimed fair comparison.

Both identify fabricated citations in the Related Work section. GT5 mentions reference [41] doesn't exist (highest is [40]); pred_id 1 identifies both [41] and [42] as non-existent fabricated citations used to support phase modeling claims.

Both identify dimensional inconsistency in ACT-PAE's phase parameter specification. GT6 notes the conflict between Q=512 and 4-dimensional [F,A,B,S]; pred_id 5 identifies the same inconsistency between R^4 scalar parameters and R^512 latent dimension.

Both identify that the claim of 'superior performance across all metrics' in long-term generation is contradicted by Table 2, where the method achieves only second-best (asterisked/italicized) performance on several metrics including MMD.

Both identify the omission of dataset limitations in Section 4.1.1's 'Remark on Dataset'. GT8 notes missing acknowledgment of demographic biases and label noise; pred_id 15 identifies the same omission of known BABEL-TEACH limitations affecting generalizability.

Both identify inappropriate promotional/marketing language in the Introduction. GT9 mentions 'revolutionary framework' and 'groundbreaking approach'; pred_id 8 identifies the same phrases as rhetorical overstatement inappropriate for academic writing.

Both identify selective metric exclusion in Section 4.1.2. GT10 notes R-precision exclusion appears motivated by unfavorable results rather than methodological soundness; pred_id 12 identifies the same exclusion of R-precision and Diversity without quantitative justification as selective omission.

Both identify a mathematical inconsistency in Equation 1's periodic signal definition. GT11 notes dimensional incompatibility in (T-S) subtraction; pred_id 4 identifies sign/argument inconsistency between equation F·T+S and prose description F·(T-S).

Both identify asymmetric inference step protocol. GT12 notes the proposed method uses 100 steps while baselines typically use 50; pred_id 14 identifies the same 100-step evaluation creating an inference-cost advantage over baselines' original 50-step settings.

Both identify overstatement of inbetweening performance in Section 4.3. GT13 notes marginal differences (e.g., 10% NPSS improvement) don't support 'superior across all' claim; pred_id 10 identifies the same issue with claimed 85% improvement not uniformly achieved across all settings.

Both identify misrepresentation of DeepPhase's contribution in Related Work. GT14 notes PAE was DeepPhase's primary contribution, not an extension; pred_id 13 identifies the same 'further extends' framing as misattribution that inflates the novelty gap.

Both identify misalignment between abstract's description and actual inbetweening method. GT15 notes phase parameters aren't 'kept fixed' but used as conditioning; pred_id 9 identifies the same contradiction between abstract's 'perfect boundary alignment' claim and the actual conditioning-based implementation.
